docs.title: Dual-Domain Galvanic Handoff Earbuds
docs.text:
A simulation-only IEEE-style paper on a true-wireless earbud platform that combines a hardware power-gated standby island with a physical lossless audio path through the stem, with the hardware designed in a narrow HDI rigid-flex stem.

Simulation-only study · hardware designed in KiCad / Cadence

TWS earbudsHDI rigid-flexPower gatingI²S audioKiCadCadence Allegro

Architecture Design constraints Source available on request

docs.title: The idea
docs.text: Mass-market true-wireless earbuds trade standby life and audio fidelity against size. This platform proposes two subsystems that live together in a narrow earbud stem:

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Subsystem What it does Key parts Hardware-enforced power-gated island Cuts standby current below 500 nA using a voltage supervisor and a load switch, with no microcontroller polling needed to decide when to wake TPS3840 supervisor, ultra-low-Ron load switch Physical lossless audio bypass Routes the stem's pogo pins through an analog switch into a digital I²S audio path, so a wired audio source bypasses the wireless link TS3A24159 dual SPDT switch, MAX98357A I²S DAC 
flowchart LR
  POGO[Stem pogo pins] --> SW[TS3A24159 dual SPDT]
  SW -->|wired mode| I2S[I²S path] --> DAC[MAX98357A] --> SPK[Driver]
  SW -->|wireless mode| BLE[BLE radio]
  BAT[Battery] --> SUP[TPS3840 supervisor] --> LS[Load switch] --> ISL[Power-gated island]

docs.title: Design constraints
docs.text: Constraint Value Form factor Narrow stem, 4.2 mm × 32 mm maximum Stackup 8-layer HDI Type-III (1+N+1 stacked micro-vias, via-in-pad) Trace / space 3 mil / 3 mil Silicon footprints 0.4 mm pitch WLCSP RF 50 Ω single-ended BLE antenna High-speed pairs 90 Ω differential, protected by a TPD4E012 ESD array
